audit_findings.title: Viper noncontrolling interests may make the numerator and denominator different claims
audit_findings.magnitude: $382 million of 2025 distributions to outside Viper holders, equal to 9.4% of the $4,080.6 million anchor; exact OE error unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated Viper cash-flow add-backs can enter OE at 100% while attributable net income and the 282.452137 million-share denominator represent only Diamondback common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, Viper paid $ 382 million, $ 227 million and $ 129 million of dividends/distributions to its public shareholders, excluding Diamondback, in accordance with the dividend policy approved by its board of directors.
audit_findings.explanation: Viper's outside ownership and the distributions owed to it are demonstrated. Whether the OE calculation allocated every Viper add-back, capital expenditure and working-capital item is unresolved. The disclosed outside distributions show a scale reasonably capable of eliminating the base case's modest premium to the $199.21 market price.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild 2025 OE by legal entity, allocating Viper operating cash flow, noncash add-backs, capital expenditures and financing costs between Diamondback and noncontrolling interests; then rerun all scenarios using only Diamondback-attributable OE.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized interest may evade the stated equity-DCF interest charge
audit_findings.magnitude: $572 million in 2025, equal to 14.0% of the $4,080.6 million anchor; exact valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized interest bypasses reported interest expense and would also bypass OE if the cash-capex deduction excludes it.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company capitalizes interest on expenditures made in connection with exploration and development projects that are not subject to current amortization.
audit_findings.explanation: The $572 million capitalization is demonstrated, but omission from OE is not: the record does not trace whether cash capital expenditures included it. If omitted, the anchor conflicts with the stated equity-OE treatment and the amount is plainly capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $572 million from cash payment through the property roll-forward and the exact capex line used in OE. Deduct it once if absent, confirm it is not later duplicated through depletion, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Material disposal gains may remain in the recurring earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $532 million pretax identified gains ($299 million EPIC, $65 million WTG and $168 million EDS), equal to 13.0% of the anchor; after-tax OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Unreversed disposal gains increase anchor OE and are then capitalized through forecast growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Other income for the year ended December 31, 2025, increased by $354 million compared to the same period in 2024, primarily due to an increase of $363 million in the gain recognized on the sale of various equity method investments in 2025 compared to 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The disposal gains are demonstrated; their inclusion in OE remains unresolved because no line-by-line normalization was supplied. Their gross scale is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion, particularly because the base value of $205.48 is only $6.27 per share above the market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each disposal to the OE worksheet, reverse the EPIC, WTG and EDS gains with their actual tax effects, retain genuine recurring investee income and post-sale service costs, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Asset-retirement cash obligations may have been added back rather than funded
audit_findings.magnitude: $547 million booked ARO at June 30, 2026; $1.1 billion undiscounted future retirement costs at December 31, 2025; recurring OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back DD&A and accretion without deducting abandonment spending or a normalized provision overstates OE; alternatively, an unfunded ARO may require a bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, our other significant contractual obligations consist primarily of (i) minimum transportation commitments totaling $3.0 billion, (ii) electrical power purchase commitments totaling $495 million, (iii) asset retirement obligations totaling $542 million, (iv) electric fracturing fleet and related power generation services commitments totaling $124 million, (v) compressor rental commitments totaling $90 million, and (vi) minimum purchase commitments for quantities of sand used in our drilling operations totaling $56 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The legal obligation is demonstrated, including $35 million of 2025 accretion and $50 million of additional liabilities. The record does not separate cash settlements from divestitures within the $153 million reduction or show what maintenance capital already funds, so neither the incremental omission nor materiality can be established without risking double counting.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the 2025 and 2026 cash plugging-and-abandonment ledger, separate settlements from divested obligations, map funded amounts into maintenance capital, and rerun with either a normalized unfunded provision or a bridge liability—not both.

audit_findings.title: The valuation perimeter does not reconcile the 2026 Viper divestiture
audit_findings.magnitude: 4,750 BO/d, equal to 0.52% of 2025 average consolidated production; $610 million final proceeds, equal to 1.05% of the $58,039 million base equity value; net OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing sold production lowers OE, debt repayment lowers prospective interest expense, and any residual proceeds affect the bridge; the effects move value in opposing directions.
audit_findings.evidence: On February 9, 2026, Viper divested all of its non-Permian assets, including those acquired from Sitio, to an affiliate of GRP Energy Capital LLC and Warwick Capital Partners LLP for net cash proceeds of approximately $617 million, subject to customary post-closing adjustments.
audit_findings.explanation: The stale operating perimeter is a demonstrated error because the February 2026 sale preceded the valuation date. However, the sold production was only 0.52% of consolidated 2025 production before allocating most of Viper to outside holders, and even the entire sale proceeds were only 1.05% of base equity value. Those conservative scale comparisons do not reasonably threaten the overall valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: For perimeter accuracy, obtain the divested properties' 2025 and January-February 2026 revenue, cash costs and attributable interest; reconcile the $610 million proceeds and repayments through the June balance sheet and confirm that neither sold earnings nor proceeds are double-counted.

audit_findings.title: Perpetual growth requires reserve-replacement capital that may exceed modeled reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: Terminal value supplies 47.7%-51.5% of scenario value; 2025 negative reserve revisions were 304.085 MBOE versus 336.178 MBOE produced; sustainable reinvestment gap unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Insufficient reserve-replacement spending makes forecast OE and the 2.5% perpetual-growth terminal value unsustainable by overstating growth available after maintenance capital.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, our proved reserves will generally decline as reserves are depleted, except to the extent that we conduct successful exploration or development activities or acquire properties containing proved reserves, or both.
audit_findings.explanation: Reserve depletion and the terminal-value dependence are demonstrated, but an actual reinvestment shortfall is unresolved. Because approximately half of every scenario depends on the terminal value, failure to fund sustainable replacement could reasonably change the valuation conclusion rather than being merely a future monitoring item.
audit_findings.action: Build a reserve roll-forward forecast linking production, decline curves, extensions, revisions and acquisitions to development and exploration spending. Determine sustainable post-reinvestment OE, including unsuccessful exploration and integration costs, and rerun the terminal period if it does not support 2.5% perpetual growth.
